operations.specification: Implements user registration (join) for the 'user' actor. This endpoint allows a new user to create an account by providing the required registration data as captured by the current schema for 'todo_list_users'. It creates a member-level user account and issues JWT access and refresh tokens upon successful registration. User credentials and registration data are validated per defined requirements and schema constraints.
operations.description:
This operation allows new users to join the application as authenticated members by registering their account in the system. The request payload must supply all mandatory fields defined in the 'todo_list_users' Prisma model, which may include credentials such as 'email', 'username', and 'password' if present. Validation and business logic ensure that all required registration data is properly checked for uniqueness (such as unique email or username), and passwords are securely handled according to best practices if the schema supports them.

Upon successful registration, the system issues both a JWT access token and a refresh token, allowing the user to authenticate further requests and refresh expired sessions securely. The tokens are returned using the standardized response DTO for the TodoList user actor, making integration straightforward for clients.

This endpoint is public, meaning no prior authentication is required to invoke it—a core requirement for initial user sign-up. The data submitted is strictly validated and stored, and appropriate error responses are sent if registration fails due to business logic violations (such as duplicate accounts or weak passwords).

The design adheres to the intended permission model for member-level users. After completion, the authenticated session context is managed per session policies defined elsewhere in your application.

Related operations involve user login and token refresh, forming the foundation of the full authentication lifecycle as captured in this API set.
operations.summary: Create a new registered user account as a member in the todo_list_users table.

requestBody.description: Data required to register a new user. Schema reflects the registration fields of the 'todo_list_users' model.

responseBody.description: JWT access and refresh tokens issued on successful registration. Format: ITodoListUser.IAuthorized.

operations.name: join

operations.specification: Implements user login for the 'user' member actor. This endpoint authenticates a user by validating their submitted credentials against the registered details stored in the 'todo_list_users' table. Upon successful authentication, issues new JWT access and refresh tokens for authenticated sessions.
operations.description:
This operation provides secure login for registered user actors. The request body requires fields typically defined in the 'todo_list_users' Prisma model, such as 'email' or 'username' and 'password', depending on the schema. The input data is strictly validated for authenticity and integrity, ensuring only correct credential pairs can authenticate.

Upon successful authentication, new JWT access and refresh tokens are issued to the user, encapsulated in the standardized response DTO for the TodoList user actor. The login process incorporates security best practices, such as hashed password comparison and failure responses for incorrect credentials, without disclosing account existence details.

No authentication is required to use this endpoint, as it is public for user login purposes. The operation's authentication flow establishes the session context for the user, controlled by session policies tied to the 'user' actor kind.

Error conditions, such as account lockouts, expired credentials, or incorrect login details, are handled by returning the appropriate error responses as per system policy and schema specification.

This login is part of the authentication workflow, typically followed by token refresh when access tokens expire. Related operations include join (registration) and refresh endpoints.
operations.summary: Authenticate a registered user in the todo_list_users table and issue tokens.

requestBody.description: Credentials for user login (usually email/username and password as defined in 'todo_list_users').

responseBody.description: JWT access and refresh tokens issued on successful login. Format: ITodoListUser.IAuthorized.

operations.name: login

operations.specification: Implements secure token refresh for authenticated 'user' actors. This endpoint allows clients holding a valid refresh token (previously issued through registration or login) to obtain a new JWT access token, maintaining ongoing session continuity without re-entering credentials.
operations.description:
This operation enables registered users to refresh their authentication tokens using a valid refresh token. The endpoint accepts a request body (or cookie, depending on architecture) containing the refresh token, and returns a new set of JWT authorization tokens.

Token refresh flow leverages the secure field design in the 'todo_list_users' table and adheres to the session and expiration policies in the business logic. This operation ensures continued access without requiring the user to re-authenticate using their credentials, following best security practices.

The endpoint is protected to accept only valid, non-expired refresh tokens. If the refresh token is missing, invalid, or expired, the operation returns an error, instructing the client to re-authenticate via login or registration.

Security is strictly enforced by using cryptographically secure token structures and adhering to server-controlled session metadata from the schema if relevant.

This completes the core authentication lifecycle together with user registration (join) and login endpoints, facilitating token rotation and long-lived authenticated user experience within permission boundaries.
operations.summary: Refresh JWT tokens for an authenticated user based on current session policies.

requestBody.description: Refresh token payload required to obtain new JWT tokens for the user.

responseBody.description: New JWT access and refresh tokens issued on successful refresh. Format: ITodoListUser.IAuthorized.

operations.name: refresh

operations.specification: This operation retrieves the detail information for a single registered user in the Todo List application. It directly queries the todo_list_users table using a unique user identifier (UUID) as a path parameter. The operation allows users and authorized systems to access individual user details including email address, account creation and update timestamps, but it never exposes password hashes or any sensitive authentication metadata. This read operation provides foundational user profile functionality, enabling secured access to self-owned user records.
operations.description:
Fetch detailed information for a specific user account in the Todo List service.

This API endpoint safely retrieves one user's profile based on their unique system-assigned identifier. Returned fields include the user's email address, the ISO 8601 timestamp when the account was created, and the most recent update time. The underlying table is todo_list_users, which ensures email uniqueness and isolates each user from others. The password hash and authentication details are never included in the API response for security reasons.

The API fully enforces access controls to ensure isolation: users may only access their own records unless extended for privileged administrative roles in the future. All error conditions—including requests for nonexistent or unauthorized users—yield clear error responses. Related endpoints may include user self-update and account deletion operations.
operations.summary: Retrieve user detail from todo_list_users by userId (UUID).

parameters.description: Unique identifier (UUID) of the user account to retrieve.

responseBody.description: Detailed user account information from todo_list_users, excluding password and sensitive credentials.

operations.specification: This operation updates user profile information for a single registered user in the Todo List application. It operates on the todo_list_users table and requires the userId (UUID) as a path parameter. The request body must conform to the ITodoListUser.IUpdate DTO schema, supporting updates to user fields such as email and password (hashed). Timestamps for updates are automatically refreshed. Password fields must be passed securely in hashed form; plaintext passwords are not accepted or stored at any stage. The operation enforces email uniqueness and never allows users to modify records they don't own. Fields not included in the request body remain unchanged.
operations.description:
Update profile information for a specific Todo List user. Only the user may update their own record; there are no cross-user operations or delegated administrative access in this system. User updates support changing email (with uniqueness enforced) and password_hash fields; all changes are subject to validation rules as described in the todo_list_users Prisma schema. Updates automatically refresh the updated_at timestamp while maintaining full audit traceability.

The operation is designed to strictly prohibit unauthenticated or cross-user modifications, rejecting any request where authentication or ownership validation fails. Error responses are descriptive in cases of conflict (e.g., duplicate email), invalid data, or permission violations. The endpoint is foundational for secure account management and is paired with endpoints for account fetch and (when required) account deletion.
operations.summary: Update a user profile in todo_list_users by userId (UUID).

parameters.name: userId
parameters.description: Unique identifier (UUID) of the user account to update.

requestBody.description: New user profile data for update. Includes only fields to be edited—supported: email and password hash.

responseBody.description: Updated user account data after the successful update, excluding password and sensitive information.

operations.specification: This operation permanently deletes a user account from the todo_list_users table. This is a hard delete operation, removing all record traces and deprovisioning associated resources. It may only be executed by system routines or administrators under exceptional circumstances (such as GDPR right to be forgotten requests or explicit deletion policy triggers). The operation ensures complete user data removal, including authentication credentials and linked session references, cascading as required by the database constraints. This endpoint is not user self-service and must not be exposed to the general user population. Deletes are not reversible; related session and secondary records are also purged as per foreign key relationships.
operations.description:
Permanently delete a user account from the system, including all authentication, ownership, and related records. Primarily used in exceptional cases such as compliance with user deletion policies, not for routine account management.

This operation is highly privileged and intended for administrative or automated routines, not for self-service by ordinary users. All associated resources owned by the deleted user will be cascaded or orphaned according to database constraints.

Security: Only users ("user" actor) according to current schema may invoke this endpoint, but should be guarded in implementation. Attempts by unauthorized actors are blocked.

Failure to find the specified userId returns a 404 error. Deletion is irreversible.

operations.specification: This operation retrieves a list of authentication session records belonging to the specified user from the todo_list_user_sessions table. It enables users ("user" actor, per schema) to view session history, including login timestamps, client IP addresses, session start/end context, and referrer data. Sessions are subsidiary to users and do not have independent business identity beyond audit and diagnostic use. The response uses a paginated structure to support efficient browsing of potentially large audit trails.
operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated, filterable list of all authentication sessions for a given user. Sessions include IP address, URL context, referrer, creation timestamp, and expiry timestamp.

This endpoint is defined to allow access by users ("user" actor), even though in normal business context it would be restricted for audit or operational support. It allows diagnosing login activity, understanding session distribution, and enforcing compliance policies. End users will see only their own sessions.

Security: "user" actor required by schema. Sensitive data such as session IPs are protected against inappropriate disclosure.
operations.summary: Session audit: Retrieve paginated user sessions (todo_list_user_sessions) by user ID.

parameters.name: userId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the target user.

requestBody.description: Session audit/search request parameters for the specified user.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of user session records associated with the user.

operations.name: index

operations.specification: This operation retrieves the details for a specific user session, identified by the owning user's unique ID and the session's unique ID. It is scoped according to the `todo_list_user_sessions` table, which is a subsidiary of `todo_list_users` and tracks authentication and access history for audit, analytics, and concurrency control. The API allows an authenticated user to review all metadata for a particular session. The fields returned include client IP, accessed/referring URLs, login/expiry times, and related user information. No operations exist for admin or cross-user querying—users may only view their own sessions. Field access, privacy, and integrity are enforced according to schema-level description and constraints.
operations.description:
Retrieve information about a single authentication session for the signed-in user. This operation is used by the account owner to view metadata related to a specific login session, which includes connection IP, originating/referring URLs, and session creation/expiry timestamps.

Access to session metadata is restricted exclusively to the user who owns the session, with permissions enforced by verifying the `userId` path parameter matches the authenticated user's identity. All fields align precisely with the `todo_list_user_sessions` Prisma schema and reference the associated user, without exposing any cross-user or admin session details.

This endpoint supports client-side session management, account security review, and personal audit. It does not allow session removal or modification—only read access limited to the valid session and its owner is granted. In cases of invalid or expired session IDs, or unauthorized access, the server will return an appropriate error response.
operations.summary: Get detailed info for a single user session from todo_list_user_sessions table

parameters.name: userId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the user who owns the session. Must match the authenticated user's ID.

parameters.name: sessionId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the specific session to retrieve, as defined in the todo_list_user_sessions table.

responseBody.description: Detailed information for the requested user session, as defined by the todo_list_user_sessions schema.

operations.specification: This operation removes (permanently erases) a specific authentication session for the requesting user, based on a composite key of user ID and session ID. It directly manipulates records in the `todo_list_user_sessions` subsidiary table, ensuring the session is owned by the authenticated user and that all permission and referential integrity checks are strictly enforced. This API does not perform any administrative or system-level session purging and is not used for forced session invalidation by external actors. Upon successful execution, the session record is deleted from the audit/history table as defined by the schema. No soft delete is performed; the operation is a permanent removal according to business and security policy.
operations.description:
Delete a user session belonging to the logged-in account. This hard-deletion operation is permitted strictly when the session belongs to the authenticated user as indicated by the `userId` path parameter.

The session identified by `sessionId` will be permanently removed from the `todo_list_user_sessions` table, eliminating all audit and metadata pertaining to that session. The operation supports use cases such as session invalidation upon logout from devices and manual removal of previous authentication records.

Security and permission enforcement are handled both at the parameter validation layer and by checking that the session belongs to the provided `userId` matching the current user's authenticated identity. If the session does not exist, is already expired, or the user attempts to access sessions belonging to another account, an error is returned. This is a hard-delete; session data is unrecoverable after execution.
operations.summary: Erase a user session from todo_list_user_sessions table for the authenticated user

parameters.name: userId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the user who owns the session. Must match the authenticated user's ID.

operations.specification: This operation fetches a list of todo items, supporting advanced searching, filtering, pagination, and sorting. It is built on the 'todo_list_todos' Prisma table, which represents user-managed todo entries. The operation uses a PATCH request allowing complex search queries in the request body, enabling filtering by fields such as status, due date, priority, and owner. Pagination and sorting options are supported to efficiently display large sets of todos. This operation is fundamental for user dashboards, lists, and search functions in the Todo List service.
operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated, filtered, and sorted list of todos from the todo_list_todos table.

The endpoint enables users to perform advanced search operations, such as filtering by owner, due dates, completion status, and priority. Request bodies may include criteria for full-text search, specific fields, or time windows. Pagination and customizable sorting are included to handle large collections and optimize performance.

Security and access control are handled so that only authorized users can access their own or permitted todo items. Public endpoints may exist for public or collaborative lists, but personal todos are restricted to their owners. Appropriate input validation and error handling are applied, and search operations are rate-limited to prevent abuse.
operations.summary: Search and retrieve a filtered, paginated list of todo items from todo_list_todos.

requestBody.description: Criteria for todo search, filtering, sorting, and pagination.

responseBody.description: Matching paginated and summarized todos in response to filter/search.

It directly maps to the 'todo_list_todos' Prisma model, providing the full set of fields and relationships present for a specific todo. A path parameter identifies the target todo, typically by its UUID. The operation supports access control so only authorized users (the owner or permitted users) can retrieve a todo item's details. This GET endpoint is essential for displaying detailed views or supporting todo update and management features.
operations.description:
Fetch full details about a single todo item from the todo_list_todos table using its unique ID.

The endpoint returns all fields and relationships for the specified todo, including title, description, status, due date, owner, and any tags or priority attributes defined in the schema. Security is enforced to ensure only owners or users with explicit permission can access the todo details. Unauthorized access is prevented, and error responses are returned for invalid or missing identifiers.

This operation underpins detail pages, edit functions, and contextual views throughout the Todo List application. The design ensures strong consistency and data integrity, with clear error handling for not-found or unauthorized cases.
operations.summary: Retrieve the complete detail of a specific todo item from todo_list_todos.

parameters.name: todoId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the target todo item.

operations.specification: This operation creates a new todo item owned by the authenticated user, based on the todo_list_todos table. The request body must provide at least a non-empty title (≤255 chars), can include an optional description (≤1000 chars), and allows an optional due date as a valid future ISO 8601 string. The completion status defaults to false (not completed). Upon creation, the todo item is linked directly to the invoking user, with lifecycle timestamps recorded automatically. All validation (required fields, type, ownership enforcement) is strictly implemented per business logic and Prisma schema, ensuring no user can create todos for another account. Only authenticated users may invoke this endpoint. The response returns the full ITodoListTodo domain DTO, including ID, status, input fields, and timestamps.
operations.description:
Create a new todo item for the authenticated user in the system.

This operation requires JWT-based authentication and checks that the incoming request comes from a valid session. The request body must contain a non-empty title of at most 255 characters; if a description is provided, it must not exceed 1000 characters. Optionally, the client may provide a due date, which must be a valid, future ISO 8601 string. The business logic enforces that ownership is attributed to the user extracted from the access token, regardless of any supplied ownership hints.

Upon successful creation, the system sets completed to false, assigns the todo to the current user, records creation and update timestamps, and persists the row with strict normalization. Any violation of field constraints, authentication, or ownership rules results in a descriptive error response, as defined in the requirements analysis.

On success, the complete todo DTO is returned, containing all main fields defined in the Prisma model, including id, title, description, completed, created_at, updated_at, and any additional business metadata as appropriate.
operations.summary: Create a new todo item in todo_list_todos owned by the authenticated user.

requestBody.description: Data for creating a new todo item, including title, optional description, and due date.

responseBody.description: The created todo item as a domain DTO.

operations.name: create

operations.specification: This operation updates an existing todo item in the todo_list_todos table for the authenticated user. It requires the todoId path parameter and a request body specifying at least one updatable field: title, description, completed, or due date. The operation ensures that only the owner of the todo may update it, enforced via the user_id foreign key and authentication context. All business validation rules apply, such as title (≤255 chars, non-empty if present), description (≤1000 chars if provided), status being a boolean, and due date being a valid future ISO string if present. The system automatically updates the modification timestamp. If the todo does not exist or is not owned by the user, an access/authorization error is returned. On success, returns the updated ITodoListTodo DTO.
operations.description:
Update an existing todo item belonging to the authenticated user.

Authentication is required. The operation checks that the todoId in the path refers to a todo owned by the calling user. The request body must specify at least one field to change (title, description, completed, or due date). Field constraints are strictly enforced: title cannot be empty or over 255 characters; description, if provided, is limited to 1000 characters; completed status is a boolean; due date, if present, must be a valid future ISO 8601 string. If the todo is not found, not owned, or request is invalid, a precise error is returned indicating the cause.

On successful update, the todo's updated_at timestamp is refreshed and the full DTO is returned. This maintains strict ownership and privacy guarantees in line with business and database requirements.
operations.summary: Update a todo item in todo_list_todos by ID, enforcing ownership and validation rules.

parameters.name: todoId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the todo item to update (UUID).

requestBody.description: Fields to update for the specified todo item (at least one must be provided).

responseBody.description: The updated todo item as a domain DTO.

operations.specification: This operation permanently deletes a todo item from the todo_list_todos table, which represents individual tasks managed by authenticated users. The operation uses the unique identifier of the todo (UUID) as the path parameter to determine which specific todo item to delete. The underlying data model enforces that only the owner user can delete their own todo; no soft deletion or history retention exists by design. Upon execution, the row is immediately and irreversibly removed from the database. This operation ensures that the business domain requirement for strict ownership and privacy of todos is maintained: only owners may perform the deletion, and once deleted, the task cannot be recovered or referenced further.
operations.description:
Permanently remove a specific todo item from the system by providing its unique identifier.

This operation allows the authenticated owner of a todo to delete their task immediately and irreversibly. Upon a successful request, the specified todo is removed from the database with no history or backup, as per system design that explicitly avoids soft deletion or task archiving.

Permission checks are strictly enforced so that only the user who owns the todo may perform this operation. Other users, including administrators, cannot delete another user's tasks. Any attempt to delete a non-existent or unauthorized todo will result in an appropriate error.

This operation directly manipulates the todo_list_todos table in accordance with its schema comments and reflects the security and privacy requirements of a personal task management system. No additional operations (e.g., recovery, status change) are triggered by this endpoint.
operations.summary: Permanently delete a todo item from the todo_list_todos table by its unique identifier.

parameters.name: todoId
parameters.description: Unique identifier (UUID) of the todo item to be deleted.

JWT access token for authenticated requests.

This token should be included in the Authorization header for subsequent
authenticated API requests as `Bearer {token}`.

This token can be used to request new access tokens when the current access
token expires, extending the user's session.

ISO 8601 date-time string indicating when the access token will expire and
can no longer be used for authentication.

refreshable_until.description:

ISO 8601 date-time string indicating the latest time until which the
refresh token can be used to obtain new access tokens.

IAuthorizationToken.description:
Authorization token response structure.

This interface defines the structure of the authorization token response
returned after successful user authentication. It contains both access and
refresh tokens along with their expiration information.

This token structure is automatically included in API schemas when the system
detects authorization actors in the requirements analysis phase. It provides
a standard format for JWT-based authentication across the generated backend
applications.

Collection of records with pagination information.

A page.

Collection of records with pagination information.

email.description: Registered email address of the user, used for unique authentication and identification within the Todo List system. Must be globally unique and is required during registration. Email is strictly validated for format compliance and checked for existing usage before allowing registration.

password.description: Plain text password to set for the account on registration. Never stored in cleartext—backend hashes this value for secure storage (mapping to 'password_hash' in the database). Passwords must meet the system's minimum strength requirements. Plain password is only accepted during registration and never exposed or returned by the API.

oneOf.description: Client IP address at the time of registration (optional). Used for security context, audit, or session management. Server may extract this if not provided.
Client IP address at the time of registration (optional). Used for security context, audit, or session management. Server may extract this if not provided.

ip.description: Client IP address from which registration occurs. Optionally supplied; if omitted, the server detects and records the connection IP address. Allows null when client IP is indeterminate.

href.description: Full URI of the registration page (current URL) used during user self-registration. This is required for session and audit context. Enables tracking of registration location and for advanced security processes. Must be supplied if the client is a browser or app.

referrer.description: Source URI that led the user to the registration page (referrer). Required for session/audit context and to understand user flows in security auditing. May be empty if the user loaded the registration page directly. Must be supplied by the client.

ITodoListUser.ICreate.description:
Data Transfer Object for registering a new member of the Todo List application. Used as the request body when creating a new user account.

This schema maps directly to the 'todo_list_users' Prisma model for core properties. The 'password' property here is the plain-text submission—handled securely by the backend (mapped to 'password_hash' in the DB). Additional fields such as registration connection metadata ('ip', 'href', 'referrer') are required for audit and compliance tracking per AutoBE standard practices.

This DTO is only used during self-registration; admin/system user creation is not supported in this API. All fields must be validated before registration, and system-generated or derived properties must not be accepted in this DTO.

id.description: The unique identifier of the new or authenticated user. Universally unique and directly maps to the 'id' of the user in the database. Must be used as the user's identity in all subsequent requests.

email.description:
Unique email address used for user authentication and identification in the Todo List application.

Email addresses must be unique among all users in the system and are validated upon registration and update. This is the only user credential exposed in the API; passwords are never returned. Used both as the login credential and the contact point for system notifications.

created_at.description:
Timestamp (ISO 8601) indicating when the user account was created.

This field is set automatically at account registration. The value is immutable and provides an audit trail for user onboarding.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp (ISO 8601) of the most recent update to the user's account profile.

This property is refreshed whenever any user information (such as email or password) is updated. It supports audit requirements and helps detect concurrent modification.

ITodoListUser.IAuthorized.description:
Response type for user registration, login, and token refresh. Encapsulates the authenticated user's identity and the JWT tokens required to authorize further requests for the Todo List application.

Returned directly by endpoints that manage user authentication as well as those that establish an authenticated session after registration or login. Client applications must extract and securely store the information from this response to enable authenticated requests and token refresh flows.

This DTO is the single point of authority for issuing, persisting, and rotating access and refresh tokens throughout the user's session lifecycle.

ITodoListUser.ILogin.description:
Login credentials and session context used by a registered Todo List user to authenticate and obtain JWT authorization tokens.

This DTO is the request body for the user login operation. It requires email (the user's unique login identifier) and raw password, both of which are strictly validated. Session context properties (href, referrer, and optional ip) record the login context for audit purposes, tracking the URL and referrer at the time of authentication.

The password field is always sent in plain text for backend-side hashing and verification, never as a hashed value in the API request. The backend will hash and compare it securely. The 'href' and 'referrer' fields are required and must be provided by the client. Optional 'ip' can be provided by the client or extracted server-side for advanced session tracking.

email.description: Unique email address for user authentication. Must be a valid and previously registered email for this Todo List user. Validated per RFC 5322 email standards.

password.description: Plain-text password associated with this user, used for credential verification at login. Never send hashed passwords in this field; only raw password should be provided for backend-side hashing.

href.description: Connection URL indicating the page from which the user attempted login (current page URL). Required for audit trails and session context tracking. Must be a valid absolute URI.

referrer.description: Referrer URL (previous page URL) from which user navigated to the login form. Required for security and session audits. May be an empty string if direct access.

oneOf.description: Optional client IP address for advanced audit and session tracking. May be omitted or set to null for standard use cases. If absent, the backend will extract from request.
Null value if client IP is not specified. Backend will extract IP server-side.

ip.description: Optional field for client-provided IP address during login. Provides enhanced session security and traceability, but is not required by standard login flows.

ITodoListUser.IRefresh.description:
Refresh token payload submitted by an authenticated Todo List user to renew JWT authorization tokens and maintain session continuity.

This DTO serves as the request body for the token refresh endpoint. Requires a valid, non-expired refresh token previously issued during login or registration. Token is validated against backend session policy and revocation checks.

No credential or session context is needed (handled via token validation and cookies). The backend processes the token securely and issues a fresh set of authorization tokens for continued user access.

refresh_token.description: A valid, non-expired refresh token issued to the user on successful login or registration. This string is required to authorize issuance of a new access token. Must be present and valid; absence or expiration triggers error response.

id.description:
Unique system-generated identifier (UUID) for the user. Serves as the primary key for user lookup, authentication, and ownership.

This property ensures that user accounts are globally unique and can be safely referenced across all relational data. It is never mutable after creation.

email.description:
Unique email address used for user authentication and identification in the Todo List application.

Email addresses must be unique among all users in the system and are validated upon registration and update. This is the only user credential exposed in the API; passwords are never returned. Used both as the login credential and the contact point for system notifications.

created_at.description:
Timestamp (ISO 8601) indicating when the user account was created.

This field is set automatically at account registration. The value is immutable and provides an audit trail for user onboarding.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp (ISO 8601) of the most recent update to the user's account profile.

This property is refreshed whenever any user information (such as email or password) is updated. It supports audit requirements and helps detect concurrent modification.

ITodoListUser.description:
Registered user account in the Todo List application (todo_list_users table).

Represents a unique system user who can authenticate, manage todos, and own their own data, with strict per-user isolation enforced. Exposes only non-sensitive fields: unique ID, email, and timestamps for account creation and updates. Never exposes passwords or authentication hashes in API responses.

email.description:
New email address to assign to the user account. Must be unique across all users in the Todo List application.

Changing this property allows the user to update their primary login credential. The new email is validated for format and uniqueness. If omitted, the email address remains unchanged.

password.description:
Plain text password provided for the purpose of updating user credentials.

This property is required if the user wishes to change their password. It is securely hashed before being persisted in the password_hash column in the database. Never store or return the plain text password. If omitted, the password remains unchanged.

ITodoListUser.IUpdate.description:
Update DTO for modifying a registered user's profile fields in todo_list_users.

Allows users to update their email address and/or password. Password is supplied in plain text and will be securely hashed by the backend for storage in the password_hash column of the database. Email changes are subject to format and uniqueness checks. At least one property must be supplied. System fields (id, created_at, updated_at) are not client editable.

ITodoListUserSession.description:
Authentication session entity for tracking user login events and access history.

Represents a single session record belonging to a user (from todo_list_users) in the Todo List application. This entity holds metadata for an authenticated session, including client IP address, login entry point (URL), referrer URL, session creation/expiry time, and a reference to the owning user. Session records support audit, diagnostics, and enforcement of session policies across the platform.

Each session is subsidiary to its owning user, providing no independent business identity aside from audit and security analytics context.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the session record. Assigned automatically by the database at creation time and guaranteed unique for each session.

Used as the primary key for referencing, updating, and deleting session records. Keeps integrity with associated user records.

user.description:
Summary of the user account that owns this session record. References the ITodoListUser.ISummary type for efficient business context and avoids the need for additional API calls to reconstruct session/user associations.

Replaces the raw foreign key `todo_list_user_id` in the response type for clarity, context, and single-call atomic operations.

ip.description: Client IP address captured at login time for session creation. Used for security analytics, audit trails, and possible anomaly detection. Required and non-nullable by schema.

href.description: URL of the page or application context where the session was initiated. Used for audit, support, and analytics. Required and non-nullable.

referrer.description: URL that referred the user to the entry/login page when starting this session. Used for historical analysis and referrer-based controls. Required and non-nullable.

created_at.description: Timestamp (RFC 3339 date-time) for when this session was established. Used for audit, support, and time-window-based controls. Non-nullable.

oneOf.description: Timestamp (RFC 3339 date-time) for when the session was closed, expired, or invalidated. Nullable for currently active or indefinite sessions.
Value is null if the session has not yet been closed or expired.

expired_at.description: Timestamp or null for session expiry; required for session lifecycle and security analytics.

ITodoListUserSession.IRequest.description:
Data structure for filtering or searching session records for a given user. Used as the request body for paginated session listing endpoints in the Todo List application.

Includes parameters for pagination, filtering by activity dates, and IP address search. All fields are optional to allow broad or fine-grained queries. Presence of these parameters restricts the returned session set. Designed for audit and diagnostic usage with fully authenticated context.

page.description:
Page number for paginated session listing.
Used for fetching specific pages of the session result set. Defaults to 1 if not provided. Must be positive.

limit.description: Maximum number of session records to include in each response page. Used for server-controlled result slicing (pagination). Default is service-administered value; recommended range is 10-100.

ip.description: Filter session records by exact client IP address. Used for IP-based investigation, anomaly detection, or audit. If omitted, no filtering by IP is applied.

href.description: Filter sessions by the login entry URL. Allows narrowing session listings to those created from a specific application or context page. If omitted, all URLs are included.

referrer.description: Filter sessions by referrer URL. Permits audit or listing of sessions started from specific referrers. If omitted, all referrers are included.

created_from.description: Minimum (inclusive) lower bound for session creation timestamp (RFC 3339 format). Allows filtering for sessions created after a certain time. If omitted, there is no lower-bound constraint.

created_to.description: Maximum (inclusive) upper-bound for session creation timestamp. Enables filtering for sessions created before or on a certain time. If omitted, there is no upper-bound constraint.

ITodoListTodo.description:
Represents a single todo item owned by a registered user of the application.

Each todo is characterized by a non-empty, required title with a maximum of 255 characters, an optional description up to 1000 characters, a boolean completion status, and automatic timestamps tracking creation and modification dates (created_at, updated_at). Every todo must belong to a unique user (user_id), which is resolved from the authenticated actor context—not accepted from API requests. No soft deletion or historical records are maintained, and todos are fully isolated by owner; only the user who created the todo may access, update, or delete it. The model does not allow for any form of user delegation, impersonation, or teaming.

No other domain entities relate to the todo except strict ownership; enforcement is via the user_id foreign key constraint to the todo_list_users model. All permissions, privacy, and CRUD operations for the MVP are governed by this core type.

id.description: Unique identifier for the todo item. Assigned automatically upon creation. Used for all retrieval, update, and deletion operations.

title.description: Title of the todo item. Must be non-empty and a maximum of 255 characters. Required for task creation and updates.

description.description: Optional detailed description of the todo item. When provided, must not exceed 1000 characters. May be omitted or null for simple tasks.

completed.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the todo item is marked as completed (true) or still pending (false). Managed entirely by the task's owner.

created_at.description: Timestamp representing when the todo item was created. Set automatically on insertion; immutable.

updated_at.description: Timestamp representing the last time the todo item was updated. Automatically refreshed on every change.

user.description: The owning user for this todo item, transformed from the internal user_id field. Always points to the authenticated actor who created and manages this task.

ITodoListTodo.ICreate.description:
The data transfer object for creating a new todo item. Used in the request body of the POST /todoList/user/todos endpoint.

This schema represents the minimal information required by business logic to create a todo owned by the authenticated user. Only the owner may create their own todos; ownership context is enforced via authentication and the backend never allows user_id to be set in the request.

Every todo must include a non-empty title up to 255 characters, optionally a description up to 1000 characters, and (if supported by business logic) an optional due date as a valid future ISO 8601 date-time string. Completion status is never accepted from the request; it is always set to false by default. All timestamps are managed automatically by the backend. Any violation of constraints will cause validation errors. The schema directly corresponds to the todo_list_todos table in the database, but strictly omits system fields, actor fields, and system timestamps from the request.

title.description: The title of the todo item. Required, must not be blank, limited to 255 characters as enforced by business rules and the database.

oneOf.description: Optional description for the todo item. If present, cannot exceed 1000 characters.
Description can be omitted or set to null if not provided.

description.description: Optional description for the todo item. Limited to 1000 characters if provided; may be null if not provided. If present, subject to all business and database constraints.

oneOf.description: Optional due date for the todo. Must be a valid ISO 8601 date-time string representing a future point in time if supplied.
Due date can be omitted or set to null if not provided.

due_date.description: Optional due date. When present, must be an ISO 8601 date-time string and must represent a time in the future. Not required; can be omitted or null.

ITodoListTodo.IUpdate.description:
The data transfer object for updating an existing todo item. Used in the request body of the PUT /todoList/user/todos/{todoId} endpoint.

Represents any subset of updatable todo fields, subject to strict validation and business rules. Used only to update the todo item owned by the currently authenticated user (user_id must never be present or accepted in the request). Each field (title, description, completed, due_date) is optional, but at least one must be provided and valid to constitute a legal update. The backend enforces all field constraints on update as with creation.

Upon successful update, the system automatically updates the updated_at timestamp and retains full ownership context. Fields with null type may be cleared by setting null, otherwise updated as allowed. All remaining fields not provided retain previous values. The schema matches updateable fields on the todo_list_todos table, excluding system-managed and actor fields.

title.description: The new title for the todo item. If provided, must not be blank and must not exceed 255 characters.

oneOf.description: The new description for the todo. If provided, cannot exceed 1000 characters.
Used to clear the description, setting it to null.

description.description: The new description for the todo item. May be updated, truncated, or cleared (set to null). Limited to 1000 characters if present.

completed.description: Completion status of the todo. True indicates completion; false indicates the task remains open. Optional and only modifiable by the owner.

oneOf.description: The new due date. Must be an ISO 8601 date-time string for a future date/time if provided.
Used to clear the due date, setting it to null.

due_date.description: The updated due date for the todo. If present, must be a valid ISO 8601 future date-time or null to clear. Optional.

ITodoListTodo.ISummary.description:
Summary DTO for a single todo item as displayed in todo list and reference contexts.

Provides essential overview information for a todo belonging to a registered user, including the unique identifier, title, completion status, and creation timestamp. Summary objects are optimized for list rendering and are included in references from other entities. All fields derive directly from the corresponding database schema with no additional aggregations or computed fields.

Used in search results, feed endpoints, and in relationship reference objects such as parent or child summaries. This type must be lightweight, omitting detailed, large, or composition-based data. Security and privacy rules are strictly enforced, ensuring no sensitive user data or internal fields are exposed.

id.description: Unique identifier for the todo item. Matches the primary key as defined in the database schema. This value is globally unique and used to reference or manipulate the specific todo item via API operations.

title.description: Title of the todo item. Non-empty, up to 255 characters in length. Required for both creation and summary display. Sourced directly from the database with validation rules enforcing non-blank strings.

completed.description: Indicates whether the todo item is marked as complete (true) or not (false). The completion state can only be changed by the owning user. This field is used for UI checkbox displays and status filtering in API queries.

created_at.description: Timestamp of when the todo was first created, as recorded in the database. This value is set by the system and is immutable post-creation. Used to sort, filter, and display historical todo activity, always in RFC 3339/ISO8601 format for proper timezone support.

user.description: Summary reference to the owning user who created and owns this todo. Only the minimal identifying properties necessary for list views and context embedding are included. Full user data is accessible via detail API calls when needed.

ITodoListTodo.IRequest.description:
Request body schema for searching and filtering todos based on flexible query criteria.

This structure supports full CRUD search, filtering, and paginated result requests for user-managed todo items. Filtering criteria include substring search in the title, completion status, and update or creation date windows. Pagination and sorting options are always present. All requests are validated to ensure users may only query their own or explicitly permitted records; no cross-user searches are ever allowed in MVP.

The schema is designed for maximum search and UI flexibility, supporting all typical dashboard and list screen user workflows. Pagination and sorting allow for scalable performance even with large todo datasets.

search.description:
Search phrase applied across the title, description, or content fields of user todos.

Supports partial (substring) matching, case insensitivity, and can be used for quick filtering in large todo collections. Useful for dashboard search features and every part of the list or filter UI.

completed.description: Filter criterion by completion status. If true, returns only completed todos; if false, only incomplete ones. If omitted, includes both completed and incomplete items. This matches all completion tracking UIs and analytics.

created_from.description:
Start datetime for filtering todos created on or after this timestamp. Must be in ISO 8601 format.

Allows the user to see todos created since a specific point in time, as may be needed for period-based report generation or activity tracking.

created_to.description:
End datetime for filtering todos created before or up to this timestamp. Must be in ISO 8601 format.

Used for retrieving todos created before a cutoff, supporting time-based reporting and analytics.

updated_from.description:
Start datetime for filtering todos last updated on or after this timestamp. ISO 8601 date-time string required.

Supports scenarios where a user needs to find recent activity or post-edit todos.

updated_to.description:
End datetime for filtering todos last updated before or up to this timestamp. Must be ISO 8601 formatted.

Helpful when narrowing recent activity searches, e.g., for audit trails or modification review windows.

page.description:
The page number of the paginated result set, starting at 1.

This allows users and UI to paginate through potentially large lists of todos efficiently. Applies usual dashboard pagination workflows.

limit.description:
The maximum number of todos to return in one page. Must be a value between 1 and 100.

Allows tuning of frontend-rendered list sizes for mobile or web views. Prevents excessive API payloads and supports UI responsiveness.

oneOf.description: Sort key for ordering the returned todo list. Can be 'created_at', 'updated_at', or 'title'.
Sort key for ordering the returned todo list. Can be 'created_at', 'updated_at', or 'title'.
Sort key for ordering the returned todo list. Can be 'created_at', 'updated_at', or 'title'.

sort_by.description:
Sort key for ordering the returned todo list. Supported values: 'created_at', 'updated_at', or 'title'.

Synchronizes with UI sort pickers and enables predictable ordering for end users.

oneOf.description: Sort order direction: 'asc' for ascending, 'desc' for descending.
Sort order direction: 'asc' for ascending, 'desc' for descending.

sort_order.description: Sort order direction for the todo list. Use 'asc' for ascending order, 'desc' for descending order. Defaults based on frontend conventions.

ITodoListUser.ISummary.description:
Summary DTO for registered todo list application users, used for lightweight identification in references and list views.

Provides only the minimal identifying fields necessary for summary context or relationship embedding. No sensitive information or internal audit fields (such as passwords, authentication tokens, or contact details) are ever included in summaries. Used in references for todo items and for embedding user context in client or API output.

Extensible for future inclusion of avatar, display name, or other public fields, but must remain minimal for performance and privacy.

id.description:
Globally unique identifier for the user account, matching the primary key constraint in the todo_list_users table.

Required for access control, resource ownership assertion, audit logging, and relationship mapping throughout the whole application context. This property never leaves summary scope—it cannot expose private details or authentication context.
